stem: The potential energy of a particle under a conservative force is given by U(x) = (x² − 3x) J. The equilibrium position of the particle is at (A) x = 1.5 m (B) x = 2 m (C) x = 2.5 m (D) x = 3 m

The force acting on an object varies with the distance travelled by the object as shown in figure. Work done by the force in moving the object from x = 2 m to x = 4 m is : [Figure: F (N) vs x (m) graph — F rises linearly from 0 at x = 0 to 4 N at x = 6 m, stays at 4 N from x = 6 m to x = 10 m, then falls linearly to 0 at x = 14 m.] (A) 4 J (B) 6 J (C) 8 J (D) 2 J
A particle moves along the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 5 m under the influence of a force given by F = 7 − 2x + 3x². The work done in the process (in J) is: (A) 70 (B) 270 (C) 35 (D) 135

In figure spring constant of the spring is 100 N/m. Extension produced in the spring is : (g = 10 m/s 2 ) [Figure: a light string passes over a fixed pulley hung from the ceiling; a 4 kg block hangs from the left end of the string, while the right end carries a light spring whose lower end holds a second 4 kg block.] (A) 10 cm (B) 20 cm (C) 30 cm (D) 40 cm
A force F̄ = (x² î + y² ĵ + z² k̂) N is acting on a particle. The particle displaces from (0, 0, 0) to (1 m, 1 m, 1 m). Find the work done by the force. (A) 1/3 J (B) 2/3 J (C) 1 J (D) 2 J

A non-Hookian spring has force F = −kx² where k is the spring constant and x is the displacement from its unstretched position. For the system shown, a mass m connected to an unstretched spring initially at rest, how far does the spring extend before the system momentarily comes to rest? Assume that all surfaces are frictionless and that the pulley is frictionless as well. [Figure: spring fixed to a wall on a horizontal top surface, string over a pulley at the edge, block on a 30° incline; x measured along the incline.] (A) (3mg/2k) 1/2 (B) (mg/k) 1/2 (C) (2mg/k) 1/2 (D) (√3mg/2k) 1/2

A locomotive of mass m starts moving so that its velocity varies according to the law v = k√s where k is constant and s is the distance covered. Find the total work performed by all the forces which are acting on the locomotive during the first t seconds after the beginning of motion. (A) W = (1/8) mk 4 t 2 (B) W = (1/4) m 2 k 4 t 2 (C) W = (1/4) mk 4 t 4 (D) W = (1/8) mk 4 t 4

The relationship between the force F and position x of a body is as shown in figure. The work done in displacing the body from x = 1 m to x = 5 m will be: [Graph of F (in N) vs x (in m), every segment 1 m wide: 0→1 ramp from 0 up to 10 N; 1→2 F = +10 N; 2→3 F = +5 N; 3→4 F = −5 N; 4→5 ramp from 0 up to 10 N; 5→6 F = 0; beyond 6 F = +5 N] (A) 30 J (B) 15 J (C) 25 J (D) 20 J

A force F = (3x²y î + x³ ĵ) N is acting on a particle. Find work done by the force when the particle moves from (1 m, 1 m) to (2 m, −1 m). [Options (B) and (D) are printed with a blank before the number; read as −5 J and −9 J] (A) 2 J (B) −5 J (C) 8 J (D) −9 J

When a spring is stretched by a distance x, it exerts a force, given by F = (−5x − 16x 3 ) N. The work done, when the spring is stretched from 0.1 m to 0.2 m is: (A) 8.1 × 10 −2 J (B) 12.2 × 10 −2 J (C) 8.1 × 10 −1 J (D) 12.2 × 10 −1 J

A force F = (3xy − 5z) ĵ + 4z k̂ is applied on a particle. The work done by the force when the particle moves from the point (0, 0, 0) to the point (2, 4, 0) as shown in the figure is [path: the curve y = x² in the x–y plane] (A) 280/5 (B) 140/5 (C) 232/5 (D) 192/5

In the shown figure, the mass m sticks to the string just after it strikes it. Then the minimum value of ‘h’, so that the lower mass bounce off the ground during its bound is: [Figure: an upper block m is held a height h above a light pan fixed to the top of a vertical spring of constant k; the lower end of the spring is attached to an identical block m resting on the ground. ‘string’ = the pan/spring top.] (A) 2mg/k (B) 3mg/k (C) 3mg/(2k) (D) 6mg/k

The potential energy function of a particle in the x-y plane is given by U = k(x + y), where ‘k’ is a constant. The work done by the conservative force in moving a particle from (1, 1) to (2, 3) is (A) 8k (B) 7k (C) −3k (D) 1k
